primary_coverage.details: All3572 extracted text lines and all310 source-manifest lines actually read,0remaining; historical38-line parse receipt also read. This is text reading for the claim/dependency map, not full independent proof verification.

Exact high-energy normalized eigenfunctions, h_j=lambda_j^{-1}, fixed compact smooth test symbols, invariant probability measure on S*M; Sigma is positive-dimensional, compact, immersed, totally geodesic and complex, with Sigma=M allowed. Support inclusion is distinguished from concentration, positive mass on Sigma and universal full support.

Assuming Theorem3.3, a missed fast orbit stays in the invariant closed complement through geodesic saturation and closure. Applying Lemma3.1 separately and taking the finite union produces a common compact V±-dense set. Theorem3.3's complete external orbit-closure proof is not audited.

Fixed smooth compact cutoff meets both orbit families. Adjoint conjugation and product rule give Op(a)*Op(a)=Op(|a|²)+O(h) in operator norm. Normalization and semiclassical convergence force the observed norm to0. Exact eigenfunctions have zero residual and satisfy the H² domain, contradicting the control estimate's fixed positive lower bound.

Projection of a support point belongs to support of the pushforward. Immersion injectivity is not required. On a connected complex curve, a positive-dimensional complex immersion has open image and compactness makes it closed; its image is M. This is the theorem conclusion's dimensional interpretation, not a new proof of the surface theorem or a certification of the higher-dimensional analytic proof for n=1.

primary_checks.claim: Invariant support gives the correct geometric alternative
hypotheses: mu is a geodesic-flow invariant probability measure on the compact cosphere bundle.
F=supp(mu) contains no S*Sigma of the stated type.
Theorem3.3 is taken as the orbit-closure input.
result: A measure-preserving homeomorphism preserves support, so U=S*M minus F is open and geodesic-invariant.
If U missed one full V+ orbit, its closed invariant complement would contain the joint geodesic/V+ orbit closure.
Theorem3.3 identifies that closure with S*Sigma, contradicting the assumption. The same argument applies to V-.
Thus U meets every complete fast orbit of both signs. This is an orbit-intersection property; topological density alone is insufficient.
primary_checks.counterchecks: Both invariance and closedness of the complement are used. A nonempty arbitrary observation set does not meet the theorem hypotheses.

primary_checks.claim: A single h-independent cutoff can observe both fast flows
result: Lemma3.1(1) separately yields compact K+ and K- inside U meeting all orbits of their respective flows.
K=K+ union K- is compact, contained in U, and meets all V± orbits.
Choose a fixed smooth symbol a equal to1 near K, with compact support in an annular neighborhood of S*M whose intersection with S*M lies in U.
This a belongs to S^0_(1,0), is independent of h, and has a nonzero set meeting both orbit families. The control constant therefore stays fixed along the sequence.
primary_checks.counterchecks: Compactness is used to get the compact orbit-hitting sets. An h-dependent choice could invalidate fixed constants and is not substituted.

primary_checks.claim: The cutoff norm vanishes in the semiclassical limit
result: The image of (4.4) confirms Op_h(a)*=Op_h(conjugate(a))+O(h). Together with (4.1), this gives Op_h(a)*Op_h(a)=Op_h(|a|²)+O(h) in L² operator norm.
Because ||u_j||=1, the expectation of the operator remainder is O(h_j).
The fixed compact smooth symbol |a|² is an admissible test in (1.3), so ||Op_hj(a)u_j||² tends to integral |a|² dmu.
mu is supported on S*M and supp(a) is disjoint from supp(mu) there, hence that integral is0.
primary_checks.counterchecks: The conjugate bar is necessary. Expectation convergence for a alone would not imply norm convergence; the |a|² product/adjoint identity supplies it.

primary_checks.claim: Exact eigenfunctions produce the contradiction in Theorem1.3
result: h_j=lambda_j^{-1} tends to0, and smooth eigenfunctions lie in H²(M).
(-h_j² Delta_g-I)u_j=0, so the entire C log(1/h_j)/h_j residual term in (4.24) vanishes.
The fixed-symbol control estimate therefore yields1<=C||Op_hj(a)u_j|| for all sufficiently large j.
This contradicts the norm limit0 and establishes the implication conditional on Theorems3.3 and4.3.
primary_checks.counterchecks: For a quasimode the residual would need its own smallness after multiplication by log(1/h)/h. No additional quasimode theorem is claimed.

result: If q lies in supp(mu), the inverse image of every neighborhood of pi(q) is an open neighborhood of q with positive mu measure.
Hence pi(supp(mu)) is contained in supp(pi_*mu). Projecting S*Sigma gives Sigma as an image, so Theorem1.2 follows.
The argument does not require an injective immersion. If no proper admissible Sigma exists, the theorem's allowed submanifold has image M, giving full support.
primary_checks.counterchecks: Inclusion of a lower-dimensional cosphere bundle in support does not imply it carries positive mu mass, nor that support equals that cosphere bundle.

primary_checks.claim: Complex dimension-one boundary, conditional geometric interpretation
result: A positive-dimensional complex immersion into a connected complex curve has the same dimension as its target and is locally a diffeomorphism.
Its image is open; a compact domain has compact, hence closed, image in the Hausdorff target.
The nonempty image is therefore all of M. Thus the support conclusion, if applied in complex dimension one, has no proper-submanifold alternative.
primary_checks.counterchecks: This is an elementary consequence of the submanifold hypotheses, not a new verification of the surface result or of every formula in the higher-dimensional geometric setup for n=1.

primary_checks.claim: Critical analytic inputs are kept explicit
result: Proposition4.9 is the uniform h^beta estimate on all long words; beta>0,0<epsilon0<1/4.
Proposition5.3 states the one-dimensional FUP with 0<=gamma1<1/2<gamma0<=1. The source attributes it to external BD18/DJN22 work.
Those inputs and the full porosity, anisotropic and Fourier-integral proof chain are read dependencies, not certified by the final support contradiction.

native_bounded_check.name: Observability/control estimate and orbit-closure alternative imply semiclassical support theorem
native_bounded_check.result: The conditional deduction is valid under the stated inputs; no substantive error found in this deduction.
actual_rederivations: Geodesic invariance of measure implies invariance of closed support and open complement.
Failure to meet a fast orbit plus geodesic invariance and closedness forces containment of a joint orbit closure, so Theorem3.3 gives the contradiction underlying Corollary3.4.
Separate compact V+-dense and V--dense sets from Lemma3.1 have a compact union giving simultaneous density.
One fixed smooth compact cutoff around that union meets the control theorem hypotheses and keeps C independent of the eigenfunction index.
The conjugated adjoint and product rules give Op(a)*Op(a)=Op(|a|²)+O(h) in operator norm; normalized semiclassical convergence makes the observed squared norm tend to zero.
Exact eigenfunctions annihilate the residual term, while the control theorem forces an observed norm bounded below by1/C.
Projection of a support point lies in spatial pushforward support; no proper admissible Sigma gives full support.
